Stage one is fully named on the packet's own face: the BCI instruction page prints "UTAH BUREAU OF CRIMINAL IDENTIFICATION, 4315 South 2700 West, Suite 1300, Taylorsville, Utah 84129" and bciexpungements@utah.gov. Stage two — the district or justice court that decided the case — is named nowhere: the 1,167-byte participant-instructions.md has no "Where you file this" section at all, and the only trace is the prefilled caption, which under this factory's settled standard is evidence but is not the instructions naming a destination. Amendment A1's test is answered first and it is answered yes: the committed track registry holds "Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence ... the participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition ... in the district or justice court that decided the case." The repository establishes it, so the packet must state it. The sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set, which ships nearly the same forms, states both stages and the 180-day window in full, so this is a gap in this packet rather than a limit of what is knowable.

SERVICE.finding: The packet states neither who must receive a copy nor how, and names no authority to ask. The 1,167-byte participant-instructions.md mentions service only twice, both times as a timing caveat — "Service method, address, date, and certification only after service occurs" and "service certifications ... remain protected" — which tells the participant when to fill a certificate in, not whom to serve. The packet does carry form 1146XX, Acceptance of Service – Expungement (Prosecutor), but a form's presence is not a direction: nothing on the delivered pages says the participant must send the prosecutor a copy, or by what method. The repository establishes the rule — the committed track registry states "The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve" — and the sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set packet states the recipient and the method in terms and names the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center (888-583-0009) besides. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Met, but only just. The instructions state where the platform stops in both required senses: they name the facts it will not supply (a ten-item list, each "supply them from your own records or complete them when the named event occurs; do not guess") and the field classes it will not sign (signatures, signature dates, service certifications, court-only, agency-only, prosecutor-only, victim fields and optional third-party authorizations). What is missing, and is recorded here rather than waved through, is the participant-facing statement that the artifact carries no approval — the sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set and ut_pet_traffic-set both carry a "What this packet is not" paragraph saying the packet is not legal advice, is not filed for the participant and decides nothing, and this one does not. The control plane does say it: approval-request.json records status REQUESTED, generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, independentVisualReviewRequired true, outputLegalApprovalRequired true, zero commercial routes opened.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The packet says the address of the court is 'not established in this repository' and sends the participant to the clerk. The repository establishes the filing rule in full, for this exact packetSetId: 'File the verified CR-409 with the proposed CR-410 at least 15 days before the hearing, in the court where the accusatory pleading was filed, or where no pleading was filed in a court with criminal jurisdiction in the city or county where the arrest occurred. One arrest per petition.' That is a two-branch venue rule, a filing deadline, and a one-arrest-per-petition limit — three answers the participant needs and the packet has. Amendment A1 decided this precise question against exactly this move: the fee standard rests on the repository not holding the figure, that fact is absent here, and 'ask the clerk where to file' substitutes a question for an answer we have. Nothing in the family directory names either venue branch, the 15-day deadline or the one-arrest limit. A participant with an uncharged arrest cannot tell from this packet which court has criminal jurisdiction over it, and a participant with two arrests is not told they need two petitions.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: The fee half is right and the waiver half is wrong, and the obligation is scored as one. The amount is genuinely open — the manifest records pay_fee as 'Unresolved and county-specific. Do not publish a figure' — so the packet is correct to publish none, correct to say why ('An unsourced figure in a filing instruction would be worse than none'), and correct to name the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the arrest as the authority who answers it. But the packet also says 'whether it can be waived … not established in this repository', and the repository answers that: the manifest's apply_fee_waiver entry names FW-001 as the general California fee waiver form, conditional on the participant being unable to pay. That is the waiver procedure, held and named, and the packet neither states it nor points at it — the string 'FW-001' does not appear anywhere in the family directory. Under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 the first question is whether the repository establishes the answer, and here it establishes half of it; a named authority may stand in only for what the record does not contain. The repair is narrow: keep the fee sentence, name FW-001.

SERVICE.detail: This is the most consequential of the three. The packet says 'who must be served and by what method … are not established in this repository' and sends the participant to the clerk. The repository establishes the whole rule: 'Serve the prosecuting attorney of the city or county where the arrest occurred, and the arresting agency, at least 15 days before the hearing.' Two named recipients and a deadline. The packet ships CR-106, the Judicial Council's own Proof of Service for criminal record clearing, and maps all 33 of its blanks — so it hands the participant the instrument for proving service while telling them the repository does not know who to serve. It is worse than a gap: the participant has the proof-of-service form, has been told the parties are unknown, and has a 15-day deadline nobody mentioned. The method half is arguably covered by CR-106's own face, which sets out service by mail and by personal delivery and points at POS-050 for electronic service; the parties and the deadline are not covered anywhere. Under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001's extension to SERVICE, a named authority stands in only where no held source establishes the rule, and one does.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states its own boundary in two places and both are true statements. The opening says these are deterministic review fixtures made from exact held official sources and are not approved filing packets, which is the most important limit and the one a reviewer most needs. The 'What this packet does not tell you' section ends by naming where self-help stops — 'fee, waiver, service, and local filing practice come from the clerk of that court, not from this packet.' Scored PASS because the obligation asks whether the packet says where it stops and sends the participant somewhere real, and it does. Noted for the repairer, though: that same sentence is the vehicle for the three failures above, so the fix must narrow what it claims is unknown rather than deleting the section, which is otherwise doing its job.

rows.repairIsNarrow: All three failures live in one paragraph of one file, participant-instructions.md under 'What this packet does not tell you'. No artifact byte needs to move, no field map changes, no source is refetched, and the nine counters stay zero. The repair is to state what the packet-set manifest already holds — the two-branch venue rule with its 15-day deadline and one-arrest limit, FW-001 as the waiver form, and the two service recipients with the 15-day deadline — and to keep the honest 'ask the clerk' only for the fee amount, which really is county-specific and unresolved.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: 'When to stop and get help' names four conditions, and the first is the honest one most packets would bury: 'you need the § 54-142a(c)(2) motion — its filing vehicle is not settled, and this packet does not draft it.' The others are the thirteen months not yet having run, the record not having been erased when it should have been (correctly sent to a different route rather than answered here), and any immigration matter, which goes to counsel without qualification. 'What this packet is not' then states that it is a guidance page with worksheets, contains no filable instrument, no caption and no signature line, is not legal advice, does not decide which branch is the participant's or whether thirteen months have run, and — a limit few packets state — that erasure is Connecticut's own remedy and nothing here describes any effect on federal or out-of-state records. It also enforces Connecticut's vocabulary rule, saying erasure rather than expungement or sealing.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the rule and corrects the mistake a participant would otherwise make. 'Who must receive a copy, and how' opens with the answer — 'You do not serve the petition yourself. The court does.' — quotes 200-00130A verbatim for it ('Once you file your petition, the court will provide a copy to the prosecutor who brough the criminal case. If your petition is already stipulated (or agreed to) by the prosecutor then the court will skip this step.'), and names the recipient and the method plainly: the prosecutor who brought the criminal case, served by the court once the participant has filed. I verified that quotation against the corpus bytes here too; it is item 4 of the official instructions, transcription error in the source and all. It then goes further than the obligation requires and heads off the specific confusion this packet creates: the State's Attorney's signature on the stipulation is not service and does not substitute for it — it is the prosecutor agreeing in advance, which is what lets the court skip the step. It also tells the participant what follows service: the prosecutor may respond, agreement may mean no hearing, opposition means one is scheduled, and failing to attend could get the petition dismissed. The repository agrees — the manifest's serve_party entry says the participant does not serve the prosecutor with process.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: CONFIRMED from the bytes, and the mechanism is visible on the page. The set reconciles perfectly — 66 requiredBeforeFiling entries in production-field-map.json against 65 instruction bullets, with no field in one and not the other in either direction (the difference is the field NYSID, required in both the application and the pro se packet, collapsing to one bullet). So nothing is missing. What is wrong is that a systematic off-by-one gives many of those blanks the name of a different blank, and it flows straight into participant-instructions.md, where the participant reads it. The field census names its own rule: nine fields on the pro se packet carry labelBasis 'printed_directly_above_in_the_same_column'. On this form the caption is printed BELOW each rule, not above it — I confirmed that by eye on raster/pro-se-packet-boundary/page-11.png, where the rules run Name of Applicant, Street Address, City State Zip, Phone, Email with each caption sitting under its own rule. So 'printed directly above' picks up the previous field's caption every time. The field census records the result in plain sight: field 'City State Zip' has effectiveLabel 'Street Address', and field 'Email' has effectiveLabel 'Phone'. Descending the certificate-of-disposition request's identifier stack, the same shift runs for nine consecutive fields and reaches the participant page as: 'Docket, Indictment, or SCI Number' for IDVNumber, 'IDV Number' for ArrestNumber, 'Arrest Number' for OrderofProtectionNumber, 'Order of Protection Number' for CertificateofDispositionNumber, 'Certificate of Disposition Number' for CriminalJusticeTrackingNumber(CJTN), 'Ticket Number' for NYSIDNumber, and 'NYSID Number' for PartialDocketNumber. A participant following that list writes their NYSID into the box captioned Partial Docket Number and their arrest number into the box captioned Order of Protection Number. Two further classes sit alongside it. Ten fields carry labelBasis 'no_printed_caption_within_reach' and reach the instruction page with no human label at all — 'Docket_Indictment_SCI_Number_2 (source field: Docket_Indictment_SCI_Number_2)', 'Sentence_Term_2', 'Release_Date_2', 'Conviction_Date_2', 'Server Address' — a raw AcroForm name presented to a participant as the words printed beside the blank. And several labels are nonsense caught mid-shift: 'Weight' for Conviction_Date, 'That' for Date_of_Service, 'By' for Court Name 2, 'I,' for Server Name, 'ATTACHMENT' for Court_Name_2, and the bare numerals 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 for Attachment_4 through Attachment_10 — themselves off by one and skipping 9. Three labels also carry raw control characters from a subsetted font, which print on the participant page as stray glyphs.
REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.repair: The off-by-one is one rule, not sixty-six edits: labelBasis 'printed_directly_above_in_the_same_column' is the wrong reading of this form's layout, where captions sit below their rules. Separately, the ten 'no_printed_caption_within_reach' fields need real labels rather than their AcroForm names, and the control characters need stripping. Do not hand-edit participant-instructions.md; it is generated from the census.

The committed track registry agrees: rules.fees gives the same no-separate-fee answer plus the $5/$10 certificate figures, the DCJS record-review fee and the notary cost, and rules.feeWaiver reads 'not applicable. There is no separate filing fee to waive.' The packet now states the held answer instead of denying it: it names the profile by path, quotes its line, and gives the full cost picture — the application free to file, so no waiver needed; the certificate of disposition at $5 outside New York City and $10 in the five boroughs, per case, with the note that a certificate is needed for each conviction being sealed and that the form itself tells the participant to ask the court about payment methods; the DCJS fee if a record review is ordered; and the notary charge, which the registry holds and which a participant would otherwise meet as a surprise at the last step. It adds that neither application source prints a fee on its face and that the silence is consistent with the rule rather than a gap in it, which I confirmed independently. This is the repair A2 asked for.

SERVICE.detail: A failure no prior lane recorded, and the plainest A1 violation in my seven families. The repository establishes who must be served, three separate times. The committed track registry, track ny_160_59_petition, holds rules.service 'Service on the district attorney with proof of service.', rules.notice 'The county district attorney, who may consent or object.', and rules.filing which ends '...and serve the county district attorney.' The national census's destination detail says the motion is 'served on the county district attorney, who may consent or object', and the census's participantFacingInstrument for this route names a service_instructions instrument outright. The packet tells the participant none of it. I searched participant-instructions.md for every relevant word — serve, service, district attorney, prosecutor — and what exists is three lines that presuppose the rule without ever stating it: 'Complete service certificates only after service actually occurs', which is a timing rule for a service the participant has not been told to perform; a list of owner-reserved field classes that includes 'prosecutor'; and 'Prior-application elections, reasons, sworn dates, service facts, prosecutor information, and notary fields remain blank.' The one operative instruction is the second bullet, which tells the participant to 'Confirm current revision, filing destination, local procedures, attachments, service, and proposed-order requirements before filing.' That is the substitution A1 forbids in as many words — a question handed back to the participant that the repository has already answered — and A2's answersVT8C4 settles that a committed manifest answering a question means the packet must not ask it. The consequence is not abstract: this is a motion the district attorney may consent to or oppose, and the packet leaves the participant to discover on their own that anyone must be served at all, while giving them eight blank service and affidavit-of-service fields to fill in.
SERVICE.repair: State it. 'Serve a copy of the motion and affidavit on the county district attorney for the county of conviction, and complete the affidavit of service after you have done so' is the held answer and costs one sentence. SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: CONFIRMED absent, with one limb of the earlier finding now spent and said so. participant-instructions.md is 92 lines and contains no self-help boundary addressed to a participant: no 'not legal advice', no statement that the packet is not filed for them, no statement that it does not decide whether the conviction can be sealed, no 'when to stop' section, and no referral to counsel. I searched for each of those. The nearest things are the opening line — 'These files are deterministic review fixtures made from exact held official sources. They are not approved filing packets' — which is a build-status disclaimer addressed to a reviewer, and the closing line, which is about release blockers. The A2 fee repair did add one sentence that touches this ground: 'the compiled profile records that legal-aid organizations and county district attorney sealing units assist pro se applicants at no cost'. So the earlier finding's 'no referral to legal aid' limb is no longer accurate and I record that rather than repeating it. It does not close the obligation: that sentence sits inside 'What it costs to file' and is offered as a cost fact — free help exists — not as a boundary on what this packet can do for the participant. What makes the gap conspicuous is how much material the repository holds to close it. The committed track registry lists ten selfHelpStopConditions for this exact track, and they are the substantive ones: any conviction that might fall on the exclusion list, including attempt or conspiracy whose target offence must be analysed; any class A felony; any single-criminal-transaction argument; district attorney objection, which converts this into a contested hearing; any pending charge; more than two convictions or more than one felony; the rehabilitation and interests-of-justice showing; immigration exposure, with the registry's own note that sealing does not remove immigration consequences and sealed records remain reachable by immigration authorities; firearms licensing goals; and federal and out-of-state convictions, which New York sealing does not reach. CPL 160.59 relief is discretionary and the eligibility arithmetic is exactly where an unaided applicant goes wrong. Six of my seven families state a boundary; this is the one that states none.
SELF_HELP_STOP.repair: Add a participant-facing boundary section carrying the registry's ten stop conditions, or a Captain-approved subset, and the ordinary three sentences the other families carry — not legal advice, not filed for you, does not decide whether the court will seal the record. The immigration condition and the district-attorney-objection condition are the two that most change what a participant should do.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.measuredHow: glyph geometry from the delivered bytes, not pixels
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Measured completely for this artifact class, and I can say why it is complete rather than partial. Every mark on every page of both fixtures is a text show: the operator census over all twelve content streams is BT/ET/q/Q/Tf/Tm/TL/T*/Tj/rg with no re, f, S, W, Do or any other path, fill, clip or XObject operator, so there is no rule, box, image or form to collide with. The single font is non-embedded /Times-Roman with /WinAnsiEncoding, which is the same standard font the composer measured with, so there is no subsetting or substitution for a raster to reveal. I extracted all 121 canonical and 126 boundary items with their exact Tm origins and measured each one with pdf-lib’s own StandardFonts.TimesRoman widthOfTextAtSize — the identical function the builder wraps at. The composer’s frame is x=72 to x=540 (612pt page, 72pt margins, maxWidth 468). Widest ink in both fixtures is x2=539.775 on page 5, "The sealing itself: $0, and no filing, because there is no filing. The compiled New York profile this route is". Zero items exceed 540. Left edge is exactly 72 on every item, top baseline 720, bottom baseline 82. No two items share a baseline with overlapping horizontal extents and no baseline pair is closer than the 14.5pt leading. The boundary fixture is the real test and it passes: a 42-character hyphenated name, a 60-character address and a 52-character email all wrap onto second lines inside the frame rather than running out of it. nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes 0 in the builder’s byte proof agrees with my independent measurement.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.whatThisDoesNotCover: A pixel render could still catch a viewer-level rendering fault that the byte geometry cannot express. That is why visualDefects is recorded as unmeasured and the verdict is held at PASS rather than PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT. This obligation is scored on what I measured; the counter is not.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: The route census names one destination for this route, "New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services", and the packet names it — "NEW YORK STATE DIVISION OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE SERVICES - RECORD REVIEW UNIT" on the face of the DCJS letter and throughout the instructions — together with the records office of the court that disposed of the case, for the workflow’s prior step. The packet also states the thing a filing-destination reader most needs on this route: there is no court to file in, because the participant files nothing. Both offices are named as offices, not gestured at. I applied the A1/A2 ask-the-repository-first test to the addresses the packet declines to state: I searched both bound records for a street address, a postcode, "Record Review" as an address context and the known Albany forms, and neither record holds an address for either office; requiredSourceIds for this census route is empty and no track registry entry or packet-set manifest holds one. The packet’s statement that the repository does not hold either address is therefore true, and it names each office as the authority that publishes its own — which is what A1 requires when the record is empty and forbids when it is not.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Scored against DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 with A1, A2, A3 and A4 all applied, and it passes each. The held answer for THIS route is stated: the compiled New York profile’s fee table carries "Automatic sealing (160.50/160.55/Clean Slate) $0 No filing", keyed to Sec. 160.55 by name, and both the delivered route sheet and the instructions print $0 and quote the line. Where the profile records an item without a figure — "DCJS record review (your own record) DCJS fee To confirm record / sealing status" — the packet says no amount is held and names the DCJS Record Review Unit as the office that publishes it, which is A1 as widened by A2. The waiver limb is answered rather than skipped: there is no fee waiver because there is no filing fee to waive, and the packet still tells a participant who cannot pay the certificate charge to ask the court’s records office and names legal-aid organisations and county district-attorney sealing units.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.a4InternalConsistency: PASS, and I tested it the way A4 asks — the delivered artifact against its own instructions. The packet prints $0, $5 and $10, and nothing in it says it does not state an amount. The four things it says it does not tell the participant are the two office addresses, the turnaround times, the DCJS record-review cost and whether a particular disposition qualifies; I checked each against the delivered pages and the instructions, and the packet states none of the four anywhere. There is no sentence of the Utah class here.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.a3PerFactPerRouteAnalysis: The one line worth arguing about is the certificate of disposition charge, $5 outside New York City and $10 within the five boroughs, whose third column in the profile reads "Required for each 160.59 case". I applied A3’s three-step test. The fact is the price the issuing court charges for a certificate of disposition; the route is the 160.55 correction submission; and the certificate is an instrument THIS route requires, because the same held record’s own note for ny_160_55_violation makes "obtain a certificate of disposition" the first step of this workflow. The $5/$10 row’s subject is the certificate itself and the annotation is the why-you-need-it column, not a scoping of the price to a statute. This is not the West Virginia shape A3 was written against, where a no-fee line keyed to 61-11-25 would have been published as the fee for a different filing under 61-11-26: there the fact was a FILING’s fee and the filings differed, here the fact is one instrument’s price and the instrument is the same one. It is also belt and braces in the packet, which states the sourced figure AND names the issuing court’s records office to confirm the current charge, so it satisfies the standard on both limbs at once and cannot mislead on either. The builder disclosed the 160.59 annotation to the participant in as many words rather than hiding it. I record this as a considered PASS with the reasoning shown, and I have raised the boundary to Captain rather than treating my reading of it as settled.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.whatIsCorrectlyNotCarriedAcross: The profile’s "CPL 160.59 sealing application No separate filing fee" line and its 160.59 filing-destination and venue rules are a different section’s answers and the packet carries none of them across. That is A3 applied correctly by the builder in the direction A3 actually forbids.

SERVICE.finding: Answered, not skipped, and answered in the only way that is true here: nobody has to be served. The route sheet says "WHO ELSE HAS TO BE TOLD — Nobody. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Stated on the delivered pages, not only in the instructions. Page 6 of both fixtures is headed "WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP" and lists six stops: a prior interests-of-justice non-sealing order, where the recorded escalation is named as a motion or counsel; a pre-November 1, 1991 disposition; wanting the courthouse file sealed, which Sec. 160.55 does not reach; a case that ended in something other than a violation or traffic infraction, with Clean Slate named as separate; either office refusing to correct; and any immigration question. The same page then states what the packet is not — not an OCA or DCJS form, not a motion, petition or application, not filed anywhere, not legal advice, not sent for you, and not a promise that either office will correct anything. The single most important negative on this route is unmissable and is repeated four times in the delivered bytes: Sec. 160.55 does not seal the court file, which is exactly the promise the controlling decision forbids.

contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.whyIDidNotFailIt: COMPONENT_SET is a completeness test — every component the route names is present — and it does not fail for carrying one more. contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.whatCaptainShouldDecide: Whether the same letter should ship from two families. contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.detail: I wrote a PDF text extractor to /tmp scratchpad; on the next read the file had been replaced by a different, more capable extractor carrying Times-Roman AFM width tables and per-item geometry. Nothing in this row rests on an unverified tool. No repository file was involved and nothing was written outside this lane’s owned path.

rows.decisiveDefect: The family declares exactly one route (obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission) and devotes pages 1-2 of 6 to court_transmission_correction_request, which is the primary instrument of a DIFFERENT declared route, obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request. That route has its own live family, its own build script and its own materially different rendering of the same letter; and the two pages here are footer-stamped with the dcjs_correction_submission route key, which in this factory's own convention is a per-document route claim.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.measuredDetail: MEASURED DEFECT, AND THE ANSWER TO THE DUPLICATION QUESTION PUT TO THIS LANE. What this family actually delivers on pages 1-2 is a two-page letter titled 'REQUEST TO THE SENTENCING COURT TO TRANSMIT OR CORRECT THE SEALING NOTICE', addressed 'TO: THE RECORDS OFFICE OF THE COURT THAT DISPOSED OF THE CASE NAMED BELOW', asking that office to transmit or correct the CPL Sec. 160.55 sealing notice. Pages 3-4 are the dcjs_correction_submission letter this family is named for and pages 5-6 the agency_route_sheet. THE DUPLICATION IS A DEFECT, and here is what I measured. (1) The sibling family composed-treatment:obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request is live in MASTER_QUEUE.json at VERIFY_PENDING, has its own build script and its own directory, and renders a 4-page packet whose pages 1-2 are ny-160-55-sentencing-court-correction-request-1 — the same act, to the same office, under the same statute. (2) The two letters are NOT the same document: the sibling's opens 'REQUEST TO THE SENTENCING COURT TO TRANSMIT OR CORRECT A CPL Sec. 160.55 SEALING NOTICE' and structures the ask as lettered sections A-C with items C1-C4; this family's opens with the express disclaimer 'THIS IS A LETTER TO A COURT'S RECORDS OFFICE. IT IS NOT A MOTION, A PETITION OR AN APPLICATION, AND IT IS NOT FILED.' and structures it as numbered paragraphs 1-4 over five separately labelled certificate-of-disposition blanks. They are two independent drafts of one instrument. (3) They do not even share a fixture persona: this family localises to '42 Larkspur Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201', the sibling prints '42 Magnolia Street, Springfield 62704' in a New York letter. (4) The convention that makes this a route-identity failure rather than a mere organisational untidiness is the factory's own: rcap-ok-custom-pleading stamps eight DIFFERENT route footers across its 24 components, one per component, so the footer is a per-document route claim. All three of this family's components carry the single footer 'Route: obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission', which means the sentencing-court letter is stamped with a route that is not its own and that a second lane holds a separate grant over. One instrument, two families, two texts, two personas, one of them wearing the other's route key, and no record in the repository reconciling them or saying which governs.

FILING_DESTINATION.measuredDetail: Two destinations, both stated and neither guessed. participant-instructions.md names letter one's destination as the records office of the court that disposed of the case ('the criminal court, city, town or village court, or the county court, whichever entered the disposition') and letter two's as the DCJS Record Review Unit, and the rendered pages address each accordingly. The packet then states plainly that the repository holds neither office's street address and that each office publishes its own — which is an honest absence rather than an A1/A2 failure, because I checked: the compiled NY profile bound by this family carries no street address for any court records office or for the Record Review Unit, so there is no repository answer being withheld. It also states there is no proceeding to file into, consistent with the bound decision's recorded rule that the participant ordinarily files nothing.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measuredDetail: Tested against DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A1/A2/A4, and it passes cleanly — this is the strongest fee treatment of the five. Where the compiled profile answers, the packet states the answer verbatim rather than sending the participant away. I re-read the profile bytes and matched each claim: the packet's 'Automatic sealing (160.50/160.55/Clean Slate) $0 No filing' is the profile's fee-table line verbatim; '$5 per case outside New York City, $10 per case within the five boroughs' is the profile's 'Certificate of Disposition (outside NYC) $5 per case' and '(within NYC) $10 per case'; and the packet even discloses the annotation those figures sit under ('Required for each 160.59 case') and explains why the charge still reaches this route. Where the profile records an item without a figure the packet says exactly that and names the office that holds it — 'DCJS record review (your own record) DCJS fee To confirm record / sealing status' is quoted and the packet says no held source states the amount. A4 satisfied: the packet nowhere claims not to state something it does state. On waiver the packet reasons rather than deflects — there is no filing fee to waive because there is no filing — and it still points to the profile's recorded free help ('legal-aid organisations and county district-attorney sealing units assist at no cost').

SERVICE.measuredDetail: 'There is nobody to serve.' The packet gives the reason rather than a bare refusal: this is correspondence with two record-holding offices and not a proceeding, so there is no opposing party, no district attorney to notify, no affidavit of service and no return date. I checked the bound records for a contrary answer and found none — the compiled NY profile records no service or notice rule for an automatic Sec. 160.55 seal, and the bound decision records the clerk, not the participant, as the party who notifies DCJS and law enforcement. The packet also supplies the operationally useful ordering rule — court letter first, DCJS letter second, because sending them the other way asks DCJS to correct a record on a notice the court has not sent — which is the bound decision's own recorded workflow order.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measuredDetail: No registry track exists for ny_160_55_violation, so the comparison basis is the hash-verified legal decision this family binds, and I read it rather than the packet's summary of it. Six stop conditions are carried, in both participant-instructions.md and the rendered agency_route_sheet: a prior interests-of-justice non-sealing order (the decision's own recorded escalation is 'motion or counsel if the court previously entered an interests-of-justice nonsealing order', and the packet reproduces that escalation and excludes the instrument); a pre-November 1 1991 disposition, matching the decision's post-1991 qualifier; wanting the courthouse file sealed, which Sec. 160.55 does not reach; a disposition other than a violation or traffic infraction; either office refusing to correct, treated as a dispute; and any immigration question. The immigration stop is present, which is the condition most often dropped. The packet also refuses the promise the decision expressly forbids — 'The product must not promise that ordinary Sec. 160.55 violations receive full court-file sealing through this section' — and says so in terms.

rows.notes: Fourteen of fifteen obligations pass on measurement and several are exemplary — the fee treatment, the blank accounting and the self-help stops are the best of the five families in this lane. The single failure is a boundary failure, not a content failure: nothing on these six pages is wrong, but two of them belong to a route this family does not hold and are stamped with one it does. The repair is a route/family boundary decision plus a footer correction, not a rewrite.

RASTER_PASS receipt: workflow run 33605354695, job 100168607212, receipt artifact id 9837602855, zip digest sha256:79fb65788c7e9c8222626b10c09dd26c5991562b3b728807db349494a69e1f4e. NO PIXEL WAS INSPECTED — artifact downloads redirect to blob storage this container's egress proxy refuses at CONNECT with 403. The receipt is cited as evidence of which bytes were rendered and where the raster lives, not of what they look like. The receipt's bound hashes were recomputed here from disk and still equal the fixtures, so the receipt has not gone stale. The receipt's runnerLine reads 'RASTER_PASS rcap-ok-custom-pleading — 2 document(s), 98 page(s) measured, 0 problem(s)', which is consistent with 49 pages across two fixtures; I did not re-read the workflow logs and record it as the receipt's assertion, not my measurement.

PAGE_ORDER.measuredDetail: 49-entry pageManifest against a 49-page pdf-lib count, differenced rather than read — the hardest page-order case in this lane and it is clean. packetPage runs 1..49 contiguously with no gap and no repeat. The 24 components appear in coherent per-track blocks, each track's primary_filing then proposed_order then filing-instructions, with each component's own sourcePage ascending inside its span and no interleaving across components. The boundary fixture carries an identical 49-entry manifest. All 49 pages measure 612x792pt with no size change mid-document. Recorded separately from COMPONENT_SET: the pages that ARE here are ordered correctly; the failure is which pages are here at all.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.measuredDetail: Word geometry taken with pdftotext -bbox-layout over both fixtures (14081 words canonical, 14113 boundary). Every same-baseline word pair whose x-ranges overlap by more than 0.25pt was enumerated and classified; the count was 0, so no pair needed classifying as either intended rendering (a value seated on the underscore/dot rule that receives it, an X inside the bracket it marks) or as a collision. Ink box [72,64.5,541.3,712.4] on a 612x792pt page: left margin 72pt, right gutter 70.7pt, top 64.5pt, bottom 79.6pt; 0 words off-page and 0 words within 18pt of any edge. This is the strongest evidence in the lane, because it is the largest surface: 14,081 canonical and 14,113 boundary words over 49 pages each, and the count of same-baseline overlapping pairs is 0 — nothing to classify as either intended rendering or collision. Uniform 72pt left margin and 70.7pt right gutter held across all 49 pages. INSTRUMENT LIMIT: this is the text layer only. It cannot see raster ink, vector rules, field borders, images, or any glyph without extractable text, and no pixel of this family was inspected.

FILING_DESTINATION.measuredDetail: Answered from the repository per route rather than deflected, and A3-correctly kept per route rather than generalised. participant-instructions.md carries eight separate FILING_DESTINATION rows, one per track, each reproducing that track's registry destination and venue. Seven read 'Oklahoma district court for the county where the arrest information is located' with the registry's notice and proposed-order detail ('The court sets a hearing and gives thirty days' notice to the prosecuting agency, the arresting agency, the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation and any other agency holding relevant records. The proposed order must identify every agency to which it applies.') and its multi-county rule. The eighth, ok_991c_deferred, correctly carries a DIFFERENT destination — 'The Oklahoma district court that entered the deferred sentence' — with its own scope limit that the order updates the court record and does not reach the arrest record held by OSBI or the arresting agency. Not reading the section 18 venue across to the 991c motion is exactly the per-route discipline A3 requires.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measuredDetail: A1/A2/A4 satisfied per route, verbatim, and this is a strong treatment. Eight FEE_AND_WAIVER rows, one per track, each reproducing that track's registry rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver word for word rather than paraphrasing or deflecting. Seven carry the full recorded answer including the figure and the payment mechanics: 'The Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation states that expunging a court record is free and that expunging an arrest record requires a $150 processing fee, which may be accompanied by fees to local law enforcement agencies. OSBI accepts cashier's checks or money orders and will not accept personal checks. The district court filing fee is not established and is recorded as an open question', with waiver 'Not established. The district court filing fee position is an open question.' The eighth, ok_991c_deferred, correctly carries its own narrower recorded text ('Not established for the section 991c motion...'). A4 is the test this most easily fails and it does not: where the registry states a figure the packet states the figure, and where the registry records an open question the packet says the question is open rather than pretending the fee is unknown in general. No fee answer was read across from one track to another.

SERVICE.measuredDetail: Answered per route from the registry. Eight SERVICE rows, seven reproducing 'By the court's notice. The proposed order must identify every agency to which it applies' together with the recorded notice rule — the court sets a hearing and gives thirty days' notice to the prosecuting agency, the arresting agency, OSBI and any other agency holding relevant records. The eighth, ok_991c_deferred, correctly carries the registry's 'Not established' rather than borrowing the section 18 answer, which is the A3 discipline again. The packet composes no service document and prints no proof of service for the participant to sign, which is right where service is effected by the court's own notice: the participant is not the serving party. The requirement that the proposed order identify every agency it applies to is disclosed, and the proposed orders leave that decision line to the court.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measuredDetail: This is the seam the lane was told to press hardest, and this family survives it completely. I took selfHelpStopConditions from the bound track registry for all eight trackIds — 52 conditions in total, seven each on ok_identity_theft, ok_18_19_deferred_dismissal, ok_18_19_felony_conviction, ok_18_19_misdemeanor_conviction, ok_18_19_nonconviction, ok_18_19_pardon and ok_vpo_60_18, and three on ok_991c_deferred — and matched every one, condition by condition, against BOTH participant-instructions.md and the text extracted from the rendered canonical PDF, normalising section signs, curly quotes and dashes and searching for each condition's distinguishing terms. Result: 52 of 52 present in the markdown and 52 of 52 present in the rendered bytes; zero dropped, zero softened, zero present in one artifact but not the other. That includes every per-track condition ('Any case where only a section 991c order has been obtained, which leaves the arrest record in place', 'Applying for the pardon itself, which is a Pardon and Parole Board matter and out of scope', 'Prosecutor no-refile confirmation, which the review records as a self-help boundary', 'Every protective order matter, until section 60.18 is read and its conditions established'), the shared SB 2030 hold, the multi-county and prosecutor-objection stops, the post-McGirt tribal-records stop, and an immigration stop on all eight tracks. Given the COMPONENT_SET failure this is worth stating plainly: the legal stop conditions were carried faithfully; what was not built was the disclosure furniture around them.

rows.notes: The largest family in this lane and the most mixed. What is here is executed to a high standard — 52 of 52 self-help stop conditions carried verbatim in both artifacts, fee, waiver, service and destination all answered per route from the registry with no cross-reading, 49 pages in correct order, zero overlaps over 14,081 words, and 56 protected fields across eight proposed orders all left empty. The failures are all of the same kind: the family declares twice the routes it serves and delivers 16 of the 53 components its own bound registry requires, and says neither. A participant on one of the eight unserved pathways is told this packet is theirs.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The repository answers this one and the packet states it. The committed registry gives destination kind court, name 'The Ohio sentencing court', detail 'Filed with the clerk of the sentencing court', and venue 'The sentencing court.' participant-instructions.md says the packet is filed 'In the Ohio court that handled the case' and names the sentencing court's own clerk as the office that supplies the caption, the form and the filing counter. The packet's added statement that no held source names a statewide Ohio filing office is accurate: the registry names a court class, not a single statewide office, and records that whether courts have published a dedicated application for a section effective March 2026 is an open question.
FILING_DESTINATION.evidence: registry destination and venue for trackId oh_marijuana_expungement; participant-instructions.md 'Where this is filed'

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: This is the decisive defect and it fails DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A1, A2 and A4 together. participant-instructions.md tells the participant, under 'What this costs': 'No held source in this packet states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or states a fee-waiver procedure' and 'This packet does not state an amount because it holds no source for one.' Both sentences are false, and the records that falsify them are the family's own. The committed track registry, which this family binds through trackId oh_marijuana_expungement, carries rules.fees 'Fifty dollars unless indigent. ORC 2953.321(G) directs thirty dollars of the fee to the state treasury, half of that credited to the Attorney General Reimbursement Fund, and twenty dollars to the county general revenue fund' and rules.feeWaiver 'Indigency excuses the fee under ORC 2953.321(G).' It also lists the fee payment and the indigency showing as required-before-filing items. Under A2 that registry is part of the repository this packet had to ask first, and under A1 a named authority to ask - here 'ask the clerk' - stands in only where the record is empty, which it is not. Worse for A4, which forbids a packet telling a participant it does not state something it does state: this packet does state it, three times inside its own directory. tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md reads 'The recorded $50 filing fee or an indigency exception ... must be confirmed against current court practice' and 'The frozen design records $50, subject to a confirmed indigency exception and current local practice'; build-findings.json carries the same sentence as a hard stop; and the canonical render report repeats it as a counsel flag. The participant-facing file denies what three sibling files in the same packet assert. The repair is to state the $50 fee and the R.C. 2953.321(G) indigency exception, keeping the confirm-with-the-clerk instruction as a currency check rather than as a substitute for the answer.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: participant-instructions.md 'What this costs'; registry rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver; tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md; build-findings.json hardStops; tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/rendered/canonical/render-report.json counselFlags

SERVICE.detail: The same A4 failure on a second fact. participant-instructions.md says 'No held source in this packet states who must be served or how. Ask the same clerk.' The registry answers the notice fact for this route: rules.notice reads 'The court notifies the prosecutor of the hearing, and the prosecutor may object by filing an objection with the court prior to the date set for the hearing. ORC 2953.321 sets no sixty-day notice period and no thirty-day objection deadline; those figures come from ORC 2953.32 and do not govern this route.' rules.service records that the section states no separate participant service duty because the court sets the hearing and the prosecutor objects to the court - which is itself an answer, and a reassuring one, not an absence. The packet withholds all of it. It never tells the participant that the court, not they, notifies the prosecutor, nor that the prosecutor may object before the hearing date. The word 'objection' appears nowhere in any participant-facing file in this family, and the track-level file again states the fact the family-level file denies, listing 'prosecutor notice' among what must be confirmed. Note for scoring: the registry's warning that the 60-day and 30-day figures belong to ORC 2953.32 and not to this route is exactly the A3 cross-reading this packet must not do, and it does not do it - the failure is omission, not substitution.
SERVICE.evidence: participant-instructions.md 'Who is served'; registry rules.notice and rules.service; grep for 'objection' across the family's participant-facing files returned nothing

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The committed registry holds nine selfHelpStopConditions for trackId oh_marijuana_expungement. The packet carries five hard stops, and four of the registry's nine are absent from every participant-facing file in the family: pending criminal proceedings or open warrants; prosecutor objection and any victim objection where applicable; choosing between sealing and expungement, which the registry calls a legal judgment with different waits and different exclusions; and immigration exposure. I grepped the family's .md and .txt files for 'warrant', 'victim', 'objection', 'sealing' and 'immigration' and none of the five terms appears in any participant-facing file. The sealing-versus-expungement omission is compounded by a second one: the registry's mechanism text names as 'the single most important disclosure in Ohio record-clearing copy' that on an expungement the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation keeps a limited record for law-enforcement employment qualification while other entities must destroy, delete and erase - so neither remedy may be described as completely gone from everywhere. No file in this family carries that disclosure. Scoring note offered honestly rather than hidden: DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 names REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, FILING_DESTINATION, SERVICE and FEE_AND_WAIVER and does not name SELF_HELP_STOP. I read the ask-the-repository-first test as reaching it, because a registry's selfHelpStopConditions are the repository's own statement of where a track's self-help ends. If Captain reads A4's list as exhaustive, this finding should be re-scored onto another obligation rather than waived - four omitted stop conditions and a missing BCI-retention disclosure are participant-safety omissions on any reading.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: THE SIGNATURE BOX OF THE FEE-WAIVER MOTION CARRIES VISIBLE INK IN BOTH FIXTURES. Packet page 4 is NHJB-2311 page 1, the Motion for Waiver of Filing Fee. Its Signature of Filer box — AcroForm field sig.8, widget /Rect [322.444, 303.983, 189.297 x 15.84], reaching the page as flattened appearance /FlatWidget-735569487 — carries the string 'Enter /s/ before name', set in /TiBo 12pt at fill 0.75 g. Rasterised here at 150 dpi it is plainly legible grey text sitting on the signature rule, directly above the printed label 'Signature of Filer'. The packet did not write it: it is the source form's own placeholder appearance, whose /TU reads '(If filing electronically, please type /s/ then your name to sign this document. Ex. /s/ John Doe)'. The field map refuses sig.8 with refusalClass signature_or_date_participant_completion and the reason 'you sign this yourself'; refusing to WRITE a field does not clear the appearance the source ships in it, and this family has no entry in data/rcap-all50/shared/field-appearance-semantics.json, so the structural default preserve_source_appearance carried it through. Under that registry's own vocabulary the correct disposition is render_participant_value_only_when_written — a placeholder is a participant input, and 'unwritten, it contributes nothing, so the source placeholder or default never reaches the filing'. This packet ships flattened, so the participant cannot make it disappear by typing: they will sign, or write /s/, over grey text that is already there. participant-instructions.md step 7 discloses it ('The signature line on NHJB-2311 already reads "Enter /s/ before name". That is the form's own instruction') and reads it as court text; the tooltip and the render-on-type behaviour say it is a placeholder, not printed form text. SECOND, INVISIBLE INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, on the sworn financial affidavit: NHJB-2328 fields 12.total, money.total and monthly.total each ship /V '0' and an appearance stream '(0.00) Tj' at fill 1 g — WHITE. The build preserved all three. On the page they are invisible: rasterised at 150 dpi the three Total lines are blank. In the delivered text layer they are not: pdftotext -layout of fixtures/canonical.pdf returns 'Total $ 0.00' three times — on the weekly take-home total (page 6, item 12), the money-presently-available total (page 6, item 13) and the monthly household expense total (page 7, item 14) — while every line feeding each total is blank. That is a sworn zero for income, for available money and for monthly expenses, extractable by any e-filing system, reader or indexer that reads the text layer of what was filed. participant-instructions.md step 6 tells the participant 'The form prints Total $ 0.00 under each column... Cross the 0.00 out and write the real total' — an instruction to strike through something that does not appear on the paper. THE REPAIR: add tx-style entries to data/rcap-all50/shared/field-appearance-semantics.json for this family — nh_petition_nonconviction_pre2019-set:NHJB-2311 field sig.8 and nh_petition_nonconviction_pre2019-set:NHJB-2328 fields 12.total, money.total, monthly.total — all four disposition render_participant_value_only_when_written, with sourceAppearanceWhenUnwritten 'Enter /s/ before name', '0', '0', '0' and the widget rects above; then correct step 6 and step 7 of participant-instructions.md, which describe an artifact that will no longer exist. This is the identical defect the TX Statement of Inability entry already documents and suppresses: 'two sworn zeroes on financial lines the participant never answered, and a date on the Option 1 declaration page beside a signature line the packet deliberately leaves blank.'

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: THE PACKET DOES NOT STATE WHERE SELF-HELP ENDS, AND THE COMMITTED RECORD THAT SAYS WHERE IT ENDS IS FULLY POPULATED. data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json holds a track nh_petition_nonconviction_pre2019 carrying eight selfHelpStopConditions (nine selfHelpBoundaries). NOT ONE OF THE EIGHT REACHES THE PARTICIPANT. Searched, by exact string and then by topic word, across every .md and .json in the family directory and across pdftotext of the delivered canonical: 0 of 8 present; the words firearm, immigration, background-check, opposition, tribal and '3 years' appear nowhere in participant-instructions.md. The instructions file has no stop section at all — its headings run 'One offence, one petition', 'Where you file this', 'What it costs', 'What you must do before you file', four per-form item tables, 'The choices that are yours', 'What the platform deliberately left blank', 'What annulment does, and what it does not do' — and the nine delivered pages are the four official forms, with no composed instructions page on which a stop could live. The nearest sentence, 'this packet does not decide whether you are eligible for one', is a disclaimer of what the packet is; it names no condition, no lawyer and no legal-aid resource. FOUR OF THE EIGHT ARE SUBSTANTIVE WARNINGS A PARTICIPANT CAN BE HARMED BY NOT HAVING: RSA 651:5, IV bars a further petition more often than every three years, so a participant who was denied within the last three years is about to spend $125 on a petition the statute bars; the annulment will not be recognised federally or for immigration; RSA 651:5, XVII says a private background-check database need not remove the record; and annulment does not restore firearm rights. THE MEASUREMENT IS COMPARATIVE, not a standard invented here: the same registry diff run against the other three official-pdf-fill families this lane holds returns in_arrest_no_charges 13 of 13 carried, ri_decriminalized 5 of 5, tx_nd_veterans_court 7 of 7. Only New Hampshire returns zero. THE REPAIR: add a 'Where self-help ends' section to participant-instructions.md carrying the eight registry conditions in the registry's own words, with a named New Hampshire legal-aid or lawyer-referral resource, in the shape the Indiana, Rhode Island and Texas families already use.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: Two held values, written and visible where they belong: participant.full_legal_name and participant.date_of_birth, in the caption of the motion (page 2) and in the caption of the affidavit (page 3), and again in the composed proposed order's caption. ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: BOTH route-determined elections are MADE on the delivered page, verified by raster rather than by text extraction — these marks are drawn as vector glyphs and no text extractor sees them. Packet page 2: 'The Defendant requests that the above-referenced case containing the following charge(s) be [X] expunged [ ] sealed' — expunged marked, sealed not; and the second decree election, 'All records and records of conviction relating to the conviction of the above-referenced case be expunged... pursuant to G.L. 1956 12-1.3-3(c) or (e)', marked. The pinned source rendered at the same crop shows BOTH boxes empty, so the marks are this packet's and are correct for a route whose committed legal name and statutory authority are an expungement. Every sworn affidavit box in every Part is left unmarked, and the composed instructions say so in terms: 'NOT ONE OF THOSE BOXES IS MARKED FOR YOU, in that Part or in any other.'

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Rasterised here at 100 dpi: every page 850x1100 px, zero dark pixels in the 18-point edge band on every page of BOTH fixtures — including the boundary fixture, whose 39-character name with a typographic apostrophe and 1972 date of birth both fit their caption cells.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: 'WHERE IT GOES. The court where the conviction occurred. File the correct court's Motion to Expunge or Seal Record with the proposed order, with the clerk of the court where the conviction occurred.' It also names the one thing the participant must pick: the motion lists four District Court judicial complexes and the packet states that it has not seen the docket and does not know which is theirs.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Stated, sourced and — importantly — qualified. Quoted from the committed record: 'No cost to the petitioner. Where the conditions of the original sentence are complete and all fines, fees and costs related to the conviction are paid in full, the court orders the expungement without cost.' The packet then reads that back to the participant rather than leaving it as a headline: the no-cost expungement is CONDITIONED on completion and on a zero balance, 'It is not a fee waiver and it does not clear an outstanding balance. ROUTE_IDENTITY.finding: Built for obligation:track-only:TX:tx_nd_veterans_court — an order of nondisclosure under Gov't Code 411.0727 after successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme — on the OCA model petition and order for that exact section. SOURCE_IDENTITY.finding: All three official sources resolve BY CONTENT HASH across the two mounted custodies. 7c34e5f5... (OCA petition, REV-2022-02) and 2c950020... (OCA order, REV-2022-02) under master_library STATES/TX/02_PACKET_FORMS; bd17a3fe... (Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs, Misc. Docket No. 22-9090) under human-source-returns/TX. COMPONENT_SET.finding: Five components, twenty-five pages, all rendered and present: the OCA petition (1-6), the OCA proposed order (7-9), a composed conditional proof of delivery to the prosecutor (10), the twelve-page Statement of Inability (11-22) and composed filing instructions (23-25). Both conditional components carry a stated condition: the proof of delivery is used only where local practice requires it, because 411.0745(e) makes the COURT responsible for notifying the State, and the Statement is used only where the participant elects it in paragraph 6 of the petition.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: Thirteen flattened widget values plus two composed-text writes, all present in the bytes and all under their own printed label: the petitioner's name in the petition caption and paragraph, in the signature block's Printed Name, on the order's Defendant line, on the Statement's 'My full legal name is', its Option 1 'My name is' and its Option 2 'Your printed name'; the phone on the petition signature block and the Statement; the address, e-mail and date of birth on the Statement; and the name on the composed proof of delivery and instructions page. Page 6 was read at the appearance level to confirm the block is the PETITIONER's — 'Respectfully submitted / Signature / Printed Name / Address / City, State, Zip / Telephone Number' — and not an attorney block; the petition carries no attorney or bar-number field at all.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: All 114 declared items carry a disclosure label that appears in participant-instructions.md, which lists them per component and then adds a 'Things the platform deliberately left blank' section naming the address split, the offence and cause number, every financial fact on the Statement, the Option 1 date and the district attorney's details.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: One route, one instrument set, and the route is stated rather than asked: the petition is the 411.0727 petition and the order the 411.0727 order, by their own printed titles. The two controls left to the participant are genuinely theirs and neither is route-determined — Dropdown6, whether evidence of completing the programme is attached (a fact about what the participant did), and Group7, whether they pay the fees or file the Statement of Inability (a financial election the platform holds no fact for). requiredOptionsMissing measured zero.

On the pages themselves: the petition's Signature widget on page 6 is an empty appearance, the order's judge, hearing and finding lines are blank, and on the Statement pages 21 and 22 the signature, the date, the county-and-state line and the whole notary block ('The notary fills out this section') are blank.

PAGE_ORDER.finding: The 25-entry page manifest matches the artifact page for page, and each official page carries its source page number and its source digest: petition source pages 1-6 to packet 1-6, order 1-3 to 7-9, proof of delivery to 10, Statement source pages 1-12 to packet 11-22, instructions to 23-25.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Measured two ways on BOTH fixtures. Rasterised here at 100 dpi: every one of the 25 pages is 850x1100 px with zero dark pixels in the 18-point edge band. Then the boundary fixture, which is where a fitter fails: its 79-character address and 58-character e-mail were measured at 150 dpi against their own widget rects on pages 12 and 21 — right-hand collar zero dark pixels in every case, with the fitter having shrunk the address to 7.5pt on page 12 and 9.5pt on page 21 to achieve it. FILING_DESTINATION.finding: 'File the petition with the CLERK OF THE COURT THAT SENTENCED YOU or placed you on community supervision', with the difference that matters named: this is NOT the county of arrest, which the committed record calls the single biggest venue difference from expunction, so a participant pursuing both may be in two different courts. evidence.destination: clerk of the Texas court that sentenced the participant or placed them on community supervision

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both stated, and the packet does something better than publish a figure: it explains why there is no statutory one. 411.0745(b) sets the TYPE of fee (the fee that generally applies to filing a civil case), not an amount, so the county's civil schedule governs; OCA describes the total as typically about $280 varying by county and tells the filer to call the clerk, and the packet repeats that instruction. It then names the number to IGNORE — the $28 that belongs only to the no-petition route under 411.072(c) — which is exactly the kind of cross-route figure a fee statement most often gets wrong. Waiver: paragraph 6 of the petition elects between paying and filing the Rule 145 Statement of Inability, which is in the packet, with the Rule 145 entitlement stated (the clerk must make the form available without charge and without being asked).

The packet therefore ships the proof of delivery as a CONDITIONAL component with 'READ THIS FIRST: YOU MAY NOT NEED THIS PAGE' printed at its head and the instruction to ask the clerk which applies in that county. No district attorney name or address is printed and the page says why.

evidence.whoServes: the court notifies the State under 411.0745(e); the proof of delivery is conditional on local practice
evidence.proofOfDeliveryCarryingInk: the petitioner's own name only; the DA name, address, method and date are blank

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Present and complete against the prescribed instrument: all 7 selfHelpStopConditions the committed legal-design track registry records for tx_nd_veterans_court are carried, in the registry's own words, and the packet adds five more of its own taken from assertions the enclosed forms actually make — including the one that decides the route, that entering the programme as a result of a DWI conviction puts the matter outside 411.0727(e) while the proposed order asks the judge to find the opposite. It also names where self-help stops for facts: the clerk for filing mechanics and the county fee, and DPS Crime Records Service for the criminal history the other-offence questions depend on.

observationsThatFailNoObligation.what: The petition's signature block splits the filer's address across two blanks (Address at rect [317.04, 552.36, 198.36 x 28.8] and City State Zip at [317.04, 504.24, 198.36 x 28.8], both packet page 6) and both are left blank, while participant.street_address — held as ONE line, '42 Live Oak Street, Austin, TX 78702' — is written twice in the same packet, on the Statement of Inability at pages 12 and 21.
observationsThatFailNoObligation.whyItIsNotAFailure: The completeness contract's availability test asks whether the platform holds a value for THE FACT the field asks for. These two blanks ask for the street part and the city/state/zip part separately, and the platform holds neither as a separate fact; splitting a one-line address by guessing where the street ends would invent structure it does not have. The refusal is declared, reasoned in those terms, and disclosed in participant-instructions.md ('Both parts of your address on the petition, because that block splits what the platform holds as one line').
observationsThatFailNoObligation.worthWatching: if the platform ever holds structured address parts, these two blanks become writable and the refusal stops being correct.

observationsThatFailNoObligation.what: The composed proof-of-delivery page (packet page 10) prints the internal route key 'Route: obligation:track-only:TX:tx_nd_veterans_court' as a footer on a page a participant may file with a court.
observationsThatFailNoObligation.whyItIsNotAFailure: It is a footer on a full, self-describing page, not a route-key-only or fragment page, and the same convention appears across composed pages in this factory.
observationsThatFailNoObligation.worthWatching: an internal identifier on a filed page is a product question, not a completeness one.

Sec. 19c'), and its footer. COMPONENT_SET.finding: The committed contract names two packet components for this route, 'Petition under Sec. 19c' and 'Trafficking nexus evidence'. The packet composes the pleading pages and says in terms which of the two is a RECORD the participant obtains rather than a page this packet can write: 'anything on that list that is a RECORD rather than a pleading is a document you obtain and file with the petition.' ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: No election control exists on any composed page, which is the correct answer for a one-route composed pleading: the petition states its statutory ground in its title, body and footer rather than printing a box to tick. The field map states the discipline explicitly — 'Where a neighbouring section of the same statute is a different route, the packet says so and tells the participant to stop rather than printing a box to tick.'

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: No signature, signature date, certificate of mailing, court-only or prosecutor-only field carries ink, and the packet says so on its own face. Nothing on this page is signed or dated for the petitioner.)'. The case-number line on page 1 is left blank and labelled 'Case number, if the court assigns one at filing'. PRINTED NAME is filled, which is correct — a printed-name line is not a signature — and the signature rule beside it is empty. Because this is a composed pleading there are no source widgets and so no source-shipped defaults to strip.

ARTIFACTS.finding: Both fixtures rehash to the sha256 and byteLength reports/rendered-artifacts.json records (12383 and 12563 bytes, 4 pages each) and both equal the digests the current raster receipt is bound to.

PAGE_ORDER.finding: The four-entry page manifest matches the artifact page for page and component for component: primary filing pages 1-2, filing instructions pages 3-4. The delivered order is petition then instructions, which is the order the manifest names.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: RAW MARKDOWN EMPHASIS DELIMITERS ARE PRINTED AS BODY TEXT ON A DELIVERED PAGE, IN BOTH FIXTURES. Re-ruled at the Captain's direction under the factory standard that CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP owns the visual appearance of the delivered page and visualDefects is its counterpart counter. My first row recorded this defect but scored it against no named obligation, on VF09's precedent for the identical defect in the WV sibling; that precedent decided only that it is not a SELF_HELP_STOP failure, which I still think is right, and it did not reach the obligation that actually owns delivered-page appearance. Under the standard as the Captain states it this is a visible defect on a delivered page and it fails here. WHAT IS ON THE PAGE: packet page 4 of 4 (612 x 792), component ok-trafficking-survivor-19c-filing-instructions-2, its own source page 2, under the heading 'WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD'. The first stop-condition bullet is drawn as a single Tj at x=72.0, baseline y=517.0, Times-Roman 11pt, black, and reads in full: '- **this is the first thing the committed record says about this route:** Oklahoma has a special'. The two delimiter pairs occupy x 78.41-89.41 and x 369.99-380.99 on that baseline. Rasterised here at 150 dpi they are plainly legible black asterisks at full body size, not faint and not marginal: the line reads '- **this is the first thing the committed record says about this route:** Oklahoma has a special'. Byte-identical in the boundary fixture at the same page, coordinates and size. pdftotext -layout returns exactly one line containing '**' in each fixture, canonical line 148 and boundary line 149. WHERE IT COMES FROM: the same string carries the same delimiters in production-field-map.json, participantFacingObligations, the SELF_HELP_STOP answer, and in participant-instructions.md, where it IS markdown and renders as emphasis correctly. The composer that writes those answers onto a composed PDF page carried the markdown source string through unrendered. WHAT THE GEOMETRY STILL PROVES, and should survive the repair: the page geometry itself is clean. Rasterised at 100 dpi, all four pages are 850x1100 px with zero dark pixels in the 18-point edge band in BOTH fixtures, ink confined to x 100-746 and y 90-985 of 850x1100, no line broken mid-token and no value overrunning its dotted rule. FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Stated with its own uncertainty named rather than papered over: the committed census records the destination as not recorded and the compiled profile records only that relief 'can be by court motion or petition' without naming the court, so the packet names the office that answers both questions — the court clerk of the Oklahoma district court for the county in which the case was filed — and prints that same description in the caption line ('IN THE ............ COURT (the Oklahoma district court for the county in which the case was filed)'). It invents no courthouse.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Stated as a refusal with an authority to ask: no committed record this packet binds states a filing fee or a fee waiver for this route, and the office that answers both is named. evidence.namedOfficeToAsk: office of the court clerk of the Oklahoma district court for the county in which the case was filed

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Present, and it is the strongest section of this packet. 'WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD' carries five stops taken from the compiled Oklahoma profile and the committed contract, led by the compiled record's own routing instruction, and the packet repeats the survivor-safety boundary in three separate places — 'Do not write a survivor narrative on this petition' on page 1, 'Do not write an account of what was done to you on any page of this packet' on page 3, and 'the facts that establish the connection are yours to tell and yours alone' on page 4. Item C6 asks the participant to IDENTIFY the trafficking-nexus evidence by document type, title or date and issuer, expressly not to narrate it. Petition page 5: the 'Respectfully submitted / Signature' rule is empty while the Printed Name and Telephone lines beneath it carry values, which is correct. ARTIFACTS.finding: Both fixtures rehash to what reports/rendered-artifacts.json records and to the queue and receipt pins: canonical 7cb3e892 645057 bytes 24 pages, boundary 2ccf4e37 645415 bytes 24 pages. pdf-lib reads 24 pages on each and every page is 612x792.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: A PARTICIPANT-FACING PAGE PRINTS AN INTERNAL ROUTE KEY THAT THE CENSUS DOES NOT CARRY, in both fixtures, on two pages. WHAT IS ON THE PAGE: packet page 9 (composed proof-of-delivery page) and packet page 24 (last instructions page) each end with the line 'Route: obligation:track-pathway:TX:tx_nd_dwi_deferred:first-offense-dwi-nondisclosure'. Drawn as body text, not a faint watermark: page 9 at xMin 104.09 yMin 629.99 xMax 466.40 yMax 639.89, page 24 at xMin 104.09 yMin 296.49 xMax 466.40 yMax 306.39, byte-identical coordinates in the boundary fixture. Rasterised here at 100 dpi, page 9 shows it plainly legible at full body size beneath the parenthetical. WHY IT IS A DEFECT: that exact string exists nowhere in this repository except this family's own builder (scripts/build-census-v1-tx_nd_dwi_deferred-set.mjs) and this family's own outputs (source-receipt.json, production-field-map.json, participant-instructions.md). The route-obligation census v1 carries this family under obligation:track-only:TX:tx_nd_dwi_deferred - in category-a-implementation-waves.json, identity-resolution/batch-2/resolved.json, source-custody-reconciliation.json and source-queue-reconciliation.json - and the family's own product-wiring.json, which is generated from the census, declares obligation:track-only:TX:tx_nd_dwi_deferred too. src/lib/legal-authority/routes/route-splits.json does not mention tx_nd_dwi_deferred at all. THE SIBLINGS SETTLE IT: all four other Texas nondisclosure families have a source-receipt routeKey identical to their product-wiring routeKey and present in the census - tx_nd_veterans_court and tx_nd_probation_misdemeanor on track-only keys, tx_nd_dwi_probation on obligation:track-pathway:TX:tx_nd_dwi_probation:first-offense-dwi-nondisclosure and tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision on its own track-pathway key, each with census hits.
