FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both are stated, both carry the controlling design's own refusal, and the owner's Q4 rule is satisfied - see the ownerCorrectionQ4 ruling on this row for the full reasoning and the quoted sentences. In summary: the guide publishes no figure of its own for either the court filing fee or the BCI application fee, states the design's refusal for each ('This packet does not publish a filing fee'; 'This packet does not publish a BCI application fee'), names the office that states each amount (the clerk of the district court where the case was heard; the Bureau of Criminal Identification at bci.utah.gov/expungements), and attributes the only two figures that appear to the enclosed forms that print them. Both waiver routes are given and correctly kept apart: the court's fee waiver via form 1305GE, which the guide says truthfully is not in this fixture and tells the participant where to get, and BCI's separate indigency waiver, which the guide says must be completed BEFORE the application is submitted, with the warning not to assume one waiver covers the other.

SERVICE.finding: THE PACKET PUTS A SERVICE OBLIGATION ON THE PARTICIPANT THAT THE CONTROLLING RECORD SAYS DOES NOT ARISE, AND OMITS THE RULE THE RECORD ACTUALLY STATES. THE RECORD, in three places and in terms: legal-design-track-registry.json track ut_pet_limitations rules.service reads 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service. The Utah Courts general service-of-process page governs first papers in a new civil case and must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have.' rules.notice reads 'The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney.' destination.detail reads 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.' THE PACKET: participant-instructions.md heads its section 'Who must receive a copy, and how' and opens 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email.' It then cites the enclosed BCI Expungement Applicant Instructions - 'after filing with the court, "Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file"' - and offers form 1146XX for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt. It adds 'Fill in the service method, the address you used and the date only after service has actually happened.' Nowhere in the file does it say that the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney, or that the petitioner does not effect service; a search for 'the court sends', 'does not serve' and 'optional' finds the rule stated nowhere. THE DEFECT IS NOT THAT THE BCI SENTENCE IS INVENTED - it is a genuine quotation from a source this family binds by hash (UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS 9e03980f) - it is that the record's primary rule is missing and its secondary, conditional route has been promoted to a flat participant duty. The consequence for a participant is real in both directions: they may believe their filing is defective until they have mailed the prosecutor, and they are given no way to know that formal service is the court's job. The Indiana sibling in this same return shows the shape that works, and shows it is available: its record says in terms 'the CCA appearance form nonetheless carries a certificate of service to the county prosecutor; follow the form', and its guide carries both limbs in the record's order. The Utah record contains no such authorisation and instead contains an express warning against importing a service regime this track does not have.

evidence.recordRule: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case
evidence.guideRule: the prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email

theTwoStillBlankColumnsOfItem1.question: Are the MCL/PACC charge-code column and the date-of-conviction column held facts the build declines to write, or facts the platform does not hold?
theTwoStillBlankColumnsOfItem1.ruling: NEITHER COLUMN IS A HELD FACT THE BUILD DECLINES TO WRITE. Both are facts the platform does not hold, for two different and separately measured reasons.
theTwoStillBlankColumnsOfItem1.chargeCodeColumn: No fact exists. I read the shared descriptor table in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs myself: it carries no MCL citation and no PACC code. matter.citation_number is a citation number, a different thing, and printing it under a heading that reads 'MCL citation/PACC Code' would state a false statutory citation to a court. There is nothing here to decline.
theTwoStillBlankColumnsOfItem1.convictionDateColumn: A descriptor exists and is reachable from nowhere, which I measured rather than accepted: matter.conviction_date is registered with requiresExplicitMapping and matches only /conviction\s*date/, and decideBinding consults protectCategoryOf BEFORE any descriptor match while PROTECT_RULES holds /\bconvict(ed|ion)\b/ under `disposition_or_hearing`. Measured in this container: protectCategoryOf('Conviction date') and protectCategoryOf('Date of conviction') both return disposition_or_hearing; decideBinding on cdate1 with explicitMappings {cdate1: 'matter.conviction_date'} returns {writable:false, reason:'protected_category'} for every label that reaches the descriptor and {writable:false, reason:'no_allowlisted_fact_matches'} for every label that does not. The two written columns get through only because their binding labels are 'Charge' and 'Case number', which the protect vocabulary does not name. So the descriptor is a schema slot no caller can fill, the fixtures accordingly carry no conviction_date, and the declaration that the platform holds none is true on these bytes. That is a shared-registry defect owned by whoever owns rcap-field-semantics.mjs — raised in build-findings.json and correctly NOT worked around by wording the binding label until the protect rule stops firing.
theTwoStillBlankColumnsOfItem1.consequence: Both columns are legitimate REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING blanks. Neither contributes to the FAIL above.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.evidence: THE FOUR THINGS THIS RE-READ WAS ASKED TO CONFIRM ALL HOLD. (1) The fourteen. A zero-write baseline was built from each pinned binary with the option ON and with it OFF. With it OFF the baseline reproduces the synthesized 14.4pt square at every one of the 14 widget rects; with it ON the baseline is pixel-identical to the pinned form at all 14. The delivered packet matches the option-ON baseline exactly: at 13 of the 14 rects the delivered dark-pixel count equals the pinned form's own, count for count (68/68, 50/50, 68/68, 72/72, 68/68, 68/68, 68/68, 70/70, 132/132, 68/68, 136/136, 136/136, 136/136), in both fixtures. Nothing is synthesized at any of them. (2) The route mark. The fourteenth rect is field 18, where the pinned form carries 68 and the delivered carries 185; the 117 extra are the family's own two diagonal strokes, plainly visible in the raster, drawn inside the widget rect. (3) Direction and location of the repair, measured against the actual pre-repair bytes recovered from history at a71d69523 (which hash 0b657ac8... and 4851f377..., confirming they are the bytes the earlier block was raised on): pages 1, 2 and 3 differ by 1176, 240 and 240 pixels in BOTH fixtures and pages 4 to 9 are PIXEL-IDENTICAL; every one of those 1656 differing pixels lies inside one of the 14 widget rects, ZERO lie outside any widget rect, ZERO lie inside a 600-00228 rect, and every change is ink LOST and none gained (1173 + 240 + 240 dark pixels removed, ~120 per widget, less where the square overlapped existing ink). pdftotext over all nine pages is character-identical before and after. (4) No other pixel moved: every pixel on every page of both fixtures that differs from the zero-write option-ON baseline falls inside a declared write box or field 18's rect, 0 outside at ZERO tolerance, and packet pages 4, 5 and 6 are pixel-identical to that baseline. THE WHOLE STANDARD ON ALL NINE PAGES THEN FINDS A DIFFERENT DEFECT, on page 5, which none of the four conditions above reaches. Reading the delivered bytes rather than a raster: each flattened widget is placed in the page content with a translation and no scale, '1 0 0 1 <x> <y> cm', and for 160 of the 161 flattened widget placements in each fixture that is correct because the appearance BBox equals the widget /Rect. For ONE it is not. 600-00228 field 15, packet page 5, is placed with '1 0 0 1 131.309 438.449 cm' while its XObject FlatWidget-1848524175 carries BBox [0 0 18 18] and strokes '0.5 0.5 17 17 re s', against a /Rect of 14.4 x 14.4 read from the pinned binary. ISO 32000-1 12.5.5 requires the transformed BBox to be mapped into the /Rect, here a 0.8 scale; it is never applied, so a 17pt stroked square is stamped where the official form draws a 13.6pt one. Rendered at 300 dpi and confirmed identically on both fixtures: the delivered box's vertical rules sit at x offsets 17.04-17.76pt from the rect's left edge when the rect ends at 14.40, and its horizontal rules at y offsets -3.60 to -2.88 above the rect's top, whereas the pinned form's own rules sit at 0.00-0.48 and 13.68-14.16, wholly inside the rect. Within 6pt of that rect the delivered page carries 802 dark pixels outside the rect against the pinned form's 132, and 670 of them are ink the official form does not carry anywhere on the page - neither in its page content nor in its own /Off stream. This is a scale-mismatch cohort question, not a Vermont one: the sweep above tested all 161 placements in each fixture by comparing every XObject BBox to its source widget's /Rect, and any family whose widget ships an appearance BBox unequal to its /Rect is exposed to the same stamp.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: FAIL on the current bytes, on packet page 5, for a defect the four confirmations above do not reach and which the FIX50 repair neither caused nor was expected to fix. It is present identically in the zero-write baseline with the option ON and with it OFF, and packet pages 5 and 6 are pixel-identical before and after the repair, so this family added nothing and FIX50 changed nothing here; FIX50's own return already names 'a widget that ships its own appearance for its current state' as one of the four cases its option deliberately leaves alone and does not close, and this is a defect inside that case. It is NOT the RI-OFF-APPEARANCE question: that determination settles that a widget's UNCHANGED /Off appearance is source-owned form structure, and this appearance is not reproduced unchanged - it is reproduced at 125% of its size. Nor is it a legal input: nothing here is for counsel to decide, because the pinned form itself shows the correct rendering and the specification states the transform. The repair belongs to the shared flattening step that emits the placement matrix, not to this family, and no route or family may be whitelisted for it.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.evidence: THE DEFECT, MEASURED THREE WAYS ON THE CURRENT BYTES. (1) THE PLACEMENT SWEEP FAILS. For every flattened widget appearance the page-content cm chain was composed through q/Q, the placed XObject's /BBox and /Matrix read, the BBox transformed by the Matrix, the placement matched to the pinned widget whose /Rect origin it translates to, and cmScale x requiredScale required to equal 1 within 0.05pt. The five are /FlatWidget-735569487, /FlatWidget-8784015711, /FlatWidget-9668333493, /FlatWidget-250812044 and /FlatWidget-1275322832 on packet page 1. Each has /BBox [0 0 18 18] and /Matrix [1 0 0 1 0 0], is placed at cmScale 1, and belongs to a widget whose /Rect is 13.68 x 13.68. requiredScale is 0.76, the product is 0.76 and not 1, and the error is 4.32pt on each axis. (2) WHAT THEY ARE. Read from the pinned JDF-477: all five are widgets of the radio group Group_6_0, the section 6 statutory-ground election -- acquitted of all charges, case completely dismissed, conviction vacated as a trafficking victim, completed diversion, completed deferred judgment. Each has /AS /Off and SHIPS ITS OWN /Off stream of 109 bytes whose content is a grey bevel, '0.501953 g 1 1 m 1 17 l 17 17 l 16 16 l 2 16 l 2 2 l f 0.75293 g 17 17 m 17 1 l 1 1 l 2 2 l 16 2 l 16 16 l f', drawn to an 18pt box. Under ISO 32000-1 12.5.5 a conforming viewer transforms that BBox by the Matrix and FITS the result onto the /Rect, so it draws the bevel at 13.68pt. pdf-lib's flatten emits a translation and no scale, so the packet stamps it at 18pt. (3) IT IS INK ON A DELIVERED PAGE, not arithmetic. Both fixtures were rastered at 300 dpi and compared pixel for pixel with the pinned JDF-477 page 1. At the five rects the delivered page paints 891/810/849/801/806 dark pixels where the pinned form paints 1060/1011/1018/1002/972, differing at 567/527/567/525/568 pixels; 1,830 of the form's own bevel pixels are lost and 924 new ones appear INSIDE the rects, and a further 2,951 dark pixels per fixture lie OUTSIDE the 13.68pt /Rect the appearance belongs to, inside the 18pt footprint, where the pinned form paints none. The overhang measures about 3.3pt to the right of each rect and about 3.3pt above it. The two fixtures are identical in this to the pixel: 3,875 added dark pixels lie outside every declared write box on page 1 of canonical and 3,875 on page 1 of boundary, of which 2,951 are outside the widget rect in each. THE REST OF THE STANDARD HOLDS, AND IS RECORDED SO THE REPAIR IS SCOPED. VF08's own defect IS discharged: all 12 widgets across the two forms whose current /AS state has no stream under /AP /N -- 5 on JDF-477 and 7 on JDF-478, which are the 24 readings VF08 counted -- are now PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the pinned form in both fixtures, so no synthesized square remains anywhere. Pages 2, 3 and 5 carry no added ink at all and are pixel-identical between fixtures and to the pinned forms; page 4 carries 23,180 (canonical) and 38,043 (boundary) added pixels and 0 of them lie outside a declared write box. FIX64 opted this builder into suppressSynthesizedAppearances and said in terms which cases the option leaves alone by design, the first being 'a widget that ships its own stream for the state it is set to'. These five are exactly that. vfASharedToolingFindings.whatThisIs: Defects VF-A found in shared tooling and shared records rather than in any one family. Recorded here because they change how other lanes' results should be read.

findings.problem: It resolves each source through its declared index path and reports 'does not bind' when that path lies in a custody the container does not mount - even when the identical bytes at the identical SHA-256 are present in a custody that IS mounted. The check immediately above it, corpus_matches_committed_index, already solves this: it excludes unmounted custodies from its sample and names them. family_sources_bind was not given the same treatment, and its own resolver comment already states the governing principle, 'ONE DOCUMENT AT TWO PATHS IS ONE IDENTITY'.
findings.observedHere: nc_145_5_felony-set reported '4 of 6 source(s) do not bind' and nc_146_acquittal_petition-set '3 of 4'. Resolving by content hash across the mounted corpus, every source of both families binds exactly. The four/three failing sourceIds declare paths under private/source-imports/rcap-d-source-packs-2026-08-12 (custody d_source_packs, not mounted here) while the same bytes sit in the mounted Master Library.
findings.consequence: Any lane reading the preflight literally will record a SOURCE_IDENTITY failure against a packet whose sources are exact. A repair lane could 'fix' a packet that has nothing wrong with it.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve a declared source by content hash across every mounted custody before reporting it unbound, and where the only copy is in an unmounted custody report NOT_MEASURABLE_HERE naming the custody, rather than a failure to bind.

findings.problem: 14 of the 350 index entries whose custody is master_library are absent from the mounted Master Library by path AND by content hash. This is not the unmounted-custody case, which the index resolver already excludes: these entries name the mounted custody itself.
findings.observedHere: CA CR-432; AL ABPP-3; MO CR310, CR143, CR370, CR311; NC AOC-CR-293, AOC-CR-293-INSTRUCTIONS, AOC-G-260; UT 1501CR, 1501CR-C, 1502CR, 1001EX, 1021EX. Because of this the preflight check corpus_matches_committed_index fails its 24-entry deterministic sample in this container (1 absent, 0 mismatched) even though master_library_complete passes at 499 files / 329 PDFs / 51 jurisdictions.
findings.consequence: Every family-scoped preflight in a container like this one reports one short and can never print the full green line, so a real regression in that check has nowhere to show.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide which record is wrong - the corpus release is short of its index, or the index names 14 assets the release never carried - and reconcile one to the other. None of the 14 is a source of any family in this cohort.

findings.problem: Passing --json still prints the human-readable table on stdout and no JSON document, so a lane cannot machine-read per-check detail such as which sources failed to bind.
findings.consequence: Every lane that needs check detail has to re-implement the resolver by hand, as this one did, which is how two lanes can measure the same obligation differently.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit the check array as JSON on stdout when the flag is set.

findings.problem: Commit cb6cbf45eca2df8befa57905b51a658859b2323f (2026-09-04, 'chore(rcap): project Virginia pardon route mapping') changed this shared ledger from 99e8029120d7... to fbf9bfef239f... without refreshing the packets that pin it. The pin was exact as of eab70f9265c837929c0b73fc208e6c5c1db80670 (2026-08-28).
findings.consequence: All six now fail SOURCE_IDENTITY on a recomputed hash. Only one of the six is in VF-A's dispatch; the other five are unclaimed by this cohort and nobody may have re-read them since the ledger moved.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-derive the six receipts together against current bytes, after confirming what changed in the manifest between the two digests. A repair lane should also consider whether a packet ought to pin a whole shared ledger file whose unrelated rows move for unrelated reasons.

findings.problem: One schemaVersion string covers at least four structurally different shapes: writes-and-refusals, documents-and-decisions, anchors-and-withheld (Washington) and maps-with-canonical-and-boundary. scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-packet-completeness.mjs handles all four deliberately, and refuses an unread schema rather than reading it as empty - which is correct. But any OTHER reader keyed to fieldMap.maps sees zero rows for a documents-shaped family and reports nine zeros over nothing.
findings.observedHere: wa_vac_felony-set is documents-shaped and carries no routeKeys and no componentSet; eleven of the twelve families in this cohort are maps-shaped. A first pass keyed to .maps read WA as 0 writes; the family in fact has 49 anchors and 33 withheld blanks, all verified.
findings.consequence: Nine zero counters from a reader that cannot parse the shape look identical to nine zero counters from a clean packet.
findings.suggestedFix: Either version the schema per shape, or require every reader to go through the same readFieldRows contract and refuse an unrecognised shape as unauditable.

findings.where: build-status.json in each family directory vs data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/RASTER_QUEUE.json
findings.problem: All twelve families in this cohort carry rasterState BUILT_RASTER_PENDING in their own build-status.json while the central RASTER_QUEUE row for each says RASTER_PASS with canonical and boundary hashes that bind to the bytes on disk.
findings.consequence: A lane that reads the per-family record applies a BUILT_RASTER_PENDING verdict ceiling that the central record has already lifted; earlier rows in these very files did exactly that.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the raster ingest write back to the per-family build-status, or make the central queue the only place a lane is allowed to read raster state from.
